newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba angered by Spanish invitation as an observer.
newsitem.headline: Cuba angered by Spanish invitation as an observer.

text.p: Cuba has angrily rejected a Spanish suggestion that it is no longer welcome as a full member at future meetings of Ibero-American parliamentarians and should attend only as an observer.

The Spanish parliament last week sent a letter to the Cuban National Assembly inviting its president to attend a future meeting of the "Conference of Presidents of Democratic Ibero-American Parliaments" in the capacity of an observer.

The president of Cuba's parliament, Ricardo Alarcon, replied that Spain was acting as if it were still the island's colonial master by trying to downgrade its status. Alarcon replied in a letter sent on Monday and made public on Tuesday.

The spat was the latest sign of tension between Madrid and the Communist-ruled island since conservative Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar took office a year ago, ending years of friendly ties under his Socialist predecessor Felipe Gonzalez.
"Nobody can ignore or discredit our full condition as a Latin American and Ibero-American nation," Alarcon said.
"It is almost one century since Cuba ceased to be a Spanish colony. Since then it has not been subject to the whims of (the Spanish) parliament," he added.

Alarcon, a senior figure in the Cuban political hierarchy and a member of the ruling Communist Party Politburo, said Cuba's parliament had participated as a full and equal member at six previous conferences of the group.

In November 1996 Havana withdrew its approval for a new Spanish ambassador, accusing Aznar's government of meddling in its internal affairs following a series of stinging criticisms of the lack of freedom in Cuba under President Fidel Castro.
